Weighted Least Squares Error (WLSE) Objective Function

Source: R/WLS.R
WLSE.Rd

Computes the total Weighted Least Squares Error (WLSE) objective function value \(f(W) = \sum_{i=1}^n \sum_{j=1}^n (w_i - a_{ij} w_j)^2\) for a given candidate priority weight vector W and Pairwise Reciprocal Matrix A (Chu et al., 1979; Yuen, 2024).

Usage

WLSE(W, A)

Arguments

W

Numeric vector of length n representing candidate priority weights.

A

Numeric square matrix of dimension n x n representing a Pairwise Reciprocal Matrix (PRM).

Value

Numeric scalar. The total Weighted Least Squares Error value.

References

Chu, A. T. W., Kalaba, R. E., & Spingarn, K. (1979). A comparison of two methods for determining the weights of belonging to fuzzy sets. Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications, 27(4), 531-538.

Yuen, K. K. F. (2024). Inverse Gram Matrix Methods for Prioritization in Analytic Hierarchy Process: Explainability of Weighted Least Squares Optimization Method. arXiv preprint arXiv:2401.01190. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2401.01190

Author

Kevin Kam Fung Yuen

Examples

# Define a 3x3 Pairwise Reciprocal Matrix
A <- matrix(c(1, 2, 5,
              1/2, 1, 3,
              1/5, 1/3, 1), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)

# Candidate priority weight vector
W <- c(0.58, 0.28, 0.14)

# Calculate WLSE objective error
err <- WLSE(W, A)
print(err)
#> [1] 0.03725378
